question: How long does a party have to cure a material breach before the other party may terminate the Agreement?
term_summary: The Agreement begins April 15, 2025, and its initial term ends at 11:59 p.m. on April 14, 2028, unless earlier terminated.
contract_basis: Section 2. Term. This Agreement begins on April 15, 2025 (the Effective Date) and continues for an initial term ending at 11:59 p.m. on April 14, 2028, unless earlier terminated under Section 8. The Agreement does not renew automatically. The parties may renew it only by signing a written renewal agreement no later than 60 days before the initial term expires. Section 8. Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement for the other party's material breach if the breach remains uncured for 45 days after the breaching party receives written notice describing the breach. If the breach is failure to pay an undisputed amount when due, the cure period is 10 days after written notice. Either party may terminate immediately by written notice if a change in law makes continued performance unlawful. Section 9. Effect of Termination. Upon expiration or termination, Customer must stop accessing the licensed service and, at Provider's election, return or destroy Provider's Confidential Information. Customer may export its stored data for 15 days after the effective date of termination, after which Provider may delete it. Undisputed fees accrued through termination are payable within 30 days. Confidentiality obligations survive for three years after termination, and accrued payment obligations and provisions that by their nature apply after termination survive. Section 11. Notices. A notice under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by personal delivery or recognized overnight courier to the recipient's legal notice address stated in the Order Form. A notice is effective when delivered.
reference_answer: The breaching party has 45 days after receiving written notice to cure a material breach. For failure to pay an undisputed amount, the cure period is 10 days after written notice.
renewal_conditions: There is no automatic renewal. Renewal requires a written agreement signed by both parties no later than 60 days before the initial term expires.
notice_requirements: Notices must be in writing and delivered personally or by recognized overnight courier to the recipient's legal notice address in the Order Form. A notice is effective when delivered. The applicable cure period is 45 days for a material breach and 10 days for failure to pay an undisputed amount.
termination_triggers: Either party may terminate for the other party's material breach if it remains uncured for 45 days after written notice; failure to pay an undisputed amount has a 10-day cure period. Either party may terminate immediately by written notice if a change in law makes continued performance unlawful.
post_termination_obligations: Customer must stop accessing the service and, at Provider's election, return or destroy Provider's Confidential Information. Customer may export stored data for 15 days after termination, after which Provider may delete it. Undisputed accrued fees are payable within 30 days. Confidentiality survives for three years, and accrued payment obligations and provisions that by their nature apply after termination also survive.

term_summary: The Agreement begins March 1, 2025, and the initial two-year term expires February 28, 2027, unless earlier terminated. It may then continue in successive one-year renewal terms.
question: Does the license renew automatically, and what must either party do to prevent renewal?
contract_basis: Section 2. Term. This Agreement begins on March 1, 2025 (the Effective Date) and continues for an initial term of two years, expiring on February 28, 2027, unless earlier terminated under Section 8. At the end of the initial term, it automatically renews for successive one-year renewal terms unless either party gives the other written notice of nonrenewal at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term. Section 8. Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 30 days after receiving written notice. Either party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or enters bankruptcy proceedings. Section 9. Effect of Termination. Within 15 days after expiration or termination, Licensee must cease using the Licensed Materials and return or destroy all copies of them and all Confidential Information in its possession, at Licensor's direction, and certify completion in writing. Fees accrued through the effective date of expiration or termination are due within 30 days. The confidentiality obligations survive for five years; provisions concerning accrued payment obligations, ownership, liability, and dispute resolution also survive. Section 10. Notices. All notices under this Agreement, including notices of nonrenewal and termination, must be in writing and delivered personally, by recognized overnight courier, or by certified mail with return receipt requested to the addresses in the signature block. A notice is effective upon delivery.
reference_answer: Yes. The Agreement automatically renews for successive one-year terms. Either party can prevent renewal by giving the other written notice of nonrenewal at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
renewal_conditions: Renewal is automatic for successive one-year terms. Either party may prevent renewal by giving written notice at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
notice_requirements: Notices, including nonrenewal and termination notices, must be in writing and delivered personally, by recognized overnight courier, or by certified mail with return receipt requested to the addresses in the signature block. Notices are effective upon delivery. Nonrenewal notice must be given at least 90 days before the then-current term ends; a material-breach notice starts a 30-day cure period.
termination_triggers: Either party may terminate for the other party's material breach if it remains uncured for 30 days after written notice. Either party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, or enters bankruptcy proceedings.
post_termination_obligations: Within 15 days after expiration or termination, Licensee must stop using the Licensed Materials, return or destroy them and all Confidential Information as directed, and certify completion in writing. Accrued fees are due within 30 days. Confidentiality survives for five years; accrued payment obligations, ownership, liability, and dispute-resolution provisions also survive.

question: After termination, may the licensee sell finished goods already in its inventory, and what conditions apply?
term_summary: The Agreement begins October 1, 2024, and the initial term ends September 30, 2025, unless earlier terminated. It may renew in successive one-year terms.
contract_basis: Section 2. Term. This Agreement begins on October 1, 2024 (the Effective Date) and continues for an initial term ending on September 30, 2025, unless earlier terminated under Section 8. It automatically renews for successive one-year terms unless either party gives the other written notice of nonrenewal at least 60 days before the end of the then-current term. Section 8. Termination. Licensee may terminate for convenience at any time after the first six months of the initial term by giving Licensor at least 30 days' written notice. Either party may terminate for the other party's material breach if the breach remains uncured for 20 days after receipt of written notice. Licensor may terminate immediately by written notice if Licensee grants an unauthorized sublicense or transfer. Section 9. Effect of Termination. On expiration or termination, Licensee must stop manufacturing new goods using the licensed marks and cease all other licensed use. If Licensee has paid all amounts due and this Agreement was not terminated because of Licensee's breach, Licensee may sell its existing finished-goods inventory for up to 90 days after the effective date of expiration or termination. During that period, Licensee must provide Licensor with a sales report each month and pay the royalties due on those sales under Section 5. At the end of the 90-day period, Licensee must stop all sales and destroy or, at Licensor's direction, return remaining goods bearing the licensed marks. Accrued royalties and other payment obligations remain payable, and confidentiality obligations survive for four years after expiration or termination. Section 11. Notices. Notices must be in writing and delivered personally or by recognized overnight courier to the notice addresses stated in the signature block. A notice is effective upon actual delivery. Email copies do not constitute formal notice under this Section. Nonrenewal notices must be delivered at least 60 days before the end of the then-current term; a convenience-termination notice must be delivered at least 30 days before its effective date; and a material-breach notice allows 20 days to cure.
reference_answer: Yes. The licensee may sell existing finished goods for up to 90 days after termination, but only if it has paid all amounts due and the Agreement was not terminated because of the licensee's breach. During that period, it must provide monthly sales reports and pay the applicable royalties. It may not manufacture new goods during the sell-off period.
renewal_conditions: The Agreement automatically renews for successive one-year terms unless either party gives written notice of nonrenewal at least 60 days before the end of the then-current term.
notice_requirements: Notices must be in writing and delivered personally or by recognized overnight courier to the signature-block notice addresses; they are effective upon actual delivery, and email copies are not formal notice. Nonrenewal notice is due at least 60 days before the then-current term ends; convenience-termination notice is due at least 30 days before its effective date; a material-breach notice provides a 20-day cure period.
termination_triggers: Licensee may terminate for convenience after the first six months of the initial term with at least 30 days' written notice. Either party may terminate for material breach uncured for 20 days after written notice. Licensor may terminate immediately by written notice for Licensee's unauthorized sublicense or transfer.
post_termination_obligations: Licensee must stop manufacturing new goods using the licensed marks and cease other licensed use. If all amounts due have been paid and termination was not due to Licensee's breach, Licensee may sell existing finished goods for up to 90 days, with monthly sales reports and payment of applicable royalties. At the end of that period, it must stop sales and destroy or return remaining marked goods as directed. Accrued royalties and other payment obligations remain payable, and confidentiality survives for four years.
